The Computer Science and Engineering department at LICET was established in 2010, focuses on providing technical education to the underserved communities. Offering a 120-student undergraduate program annually, the department actively collaborates with industries, facilitating student exposure and bridging the academia-industry gap.

Faculty and students have developed and maintained various software applications, including Performance Evaluation System, Apps for Education, Learning Management System (Moodle), and campus-wide networking activities. National-level technical events like Oracle Technology Network Yatra and Srinivasa Ramanujan Mathematical Competition are organized. The department manages G-Suite for education, offers Red Hat Academy certification programs, and engages in initiatives like NMEICT, Faculty Development Programmes, and Aakash R&D, receiving a grant of around 20 lakhs.

Students have excelled in innovative projects such as Project AR Labs, Implantable Hearing Machine, and Project MicrOS. Noteworthy contributions include software for campus management, attendance helpline, and online tests. Alumni find placements in leading companies like Infosys, Tech Mahindra, SAP, and Vernalis. Through the ICAM MoU, 10 to 15 students, accompanied by a faculty member, annually undertake technical projects at ICAM campuses in France.

The department of Computer Science and Engineering has been recognized as a research centre for collaborative research with Anna University and to guide Ph.D scholars to carry out research in their area of interest.
To Form competent Computing Engineers who are motivated towards Innovation and Collaborative Research, To Serve the ever changing needs of the Society.

• To inculcate learnability skills in the student to acquire knowledge in the fundamentals of Computer Science and Engineering.
  • To bring out the creativeness in the mind of the student leading to innovation and research.
  • To develop professional skills and adaptiveness through collaborative activities.
  • To create awareness on ethical values and involve the student to serve the societal needs.

The Departmental Association, EICON – Engineers Integrated for Computing Needs, was inaugurated on 11th February 2013, with Shri A. K. Pattabiraman, Head – Accreditation Process, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), as the Chief Guest. EICON remains the heartbeat of student activities—organising hackathons, coding sprints, guest lectures, and cultural-technical fests that keep campus life dynamic. Under the auspices of EICON, the technical symposium Xplore ’13 was organized and inaugurated by Mr. Sujith Kumar, Infosys Ltd., Chennai. The symposium has since been conducted annually, fostering analytical thinking, technical proficiency, teamwork, and innovation among participants from various engineering institutions.

The department received the Higher Education Excellence Award in 2019 from Staffordshire University, UK, and Education Matters. The department received NBA accreditation in 2019, and its intake was increased to 120 students from 2022 onwards.The department was recognized as an Anna University Research Department in 2024.

A total of 18 students have secured University Ranks at Anna University over the years, including an Anna University Gold Medalist, Ms. Hancy Jose. Ms. Nisha Maria Arun Kumar was honored with the ISTE Tamil Nadu Section Best Student Award for the year 2017.

The department has received ₹29,364,835 through funded programs and ₹4,59,935 through self-supported funding, which includes ₹2,97,885 in support from TNSDC, TNSCST, and TANCOM. Faculty members and students have contributed to over 80 research publications and have collectively organized more than 300 workshops and events. The department has also facilitated the incubation of two start-ups, Hospitintel and CareConnect AI.

About 150 students have participated in an international summer internship program with Institut catholique d’arts et métiers (ICAM), experiencing project-based learning across Paris, Lille, Toulouse, and Nantes. The program blends academic rigor with industrial exposure, intercultural collaboration, and language learning. This international exposure builds cross-cultural competence, industry-ready skills, and a global mindset—qualities that employers value highly.

The department’s industry ties include Red Hat Academy, AWS Academy, DTCC, VMware, Google Academy, Bharat Block chain, XRIT, Oracle Academy and others. These partnerships power curriculum enrichment, certification pathways, and hands-on workshops. Over 300 workshops, guest lectures, and project events have been hosted, driven by industry experts and academic leaders. These events keep students current with emerging technologies and practical tools.

Beyond academics, the department has nurtured 20 international sports players across table tennis, swimming, cricket, badminton, football, and volleyball. These student-athletes have represented the college, state, and nation—showcasing the department’s commitment to balanced growth.

Approximately 700 alumni are employed across multinational companies worldwide, occupying roles that reflect technical competence and leadership. Alumni success stories reinforce the department’s reputation and create a virtuous cycle of mentorship and recruitment.

blocks.html: Engineering graduates will be able to
PSO 1 – Apply software engineering principles and practices for developing quality software for scientific and business applications.
PSO 2 – Adapt to emerging Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) to innovate ideas and solutions to existing novel problems.
PSO 3 – Attain excellence in emerging fields of Machine Learning and Data Science.

PO1 – Engineering Knowledge: Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering problems.

PO2 – Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1 to WK4)

PO3 – Design/Development of Solutions: Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5)

PO4 – Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8).

PO5 – Engineering Tool Usage: Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering & IT tools, including prediction and modelling recognizing their limitations to solve complex engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6)

PO6 – The Engineer and The World: Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7).
PO7 – Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws. (WK9)
PO8 – Individual and Collaborative Team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams.

PO9 – Communication: Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences

PO10 – Project Management and Finance: Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

PO11 – Life-Long Learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8)

KNOWLEDGE AND ATTITUDE PROFILE (WK)

WK1 – A systematic, theory-based understanding of the natural sciences applicable to the discipline and awareness of relevant social sciences.

WK2 – Conceptually-based mathematics, numerical analysis, data analysis, statistics and formal aspects of computer and information science to support detailed analysis and modelling applicable to the discipline.
WK3 – A systematic, theory-based formulation of engineering fundamentals required in the engineering discipline.

WK4 – Engineering specialist knowledge that provides theoretical frameworks and bodies of knowledge for the accepted practice areas in the engineering discipline; much is at the forefront of the discipline.

WK5 – Knowledge, including efficient resource use, environmental impacts, whole-life cost, re-use of resources, net zero carbon, and similar concepts, that supports engineering design and operations in a practice area.
WK6 – Knowledge of engineering practice (technology) in the practice areas in the engineering discipline.

WK7 – Knowledge of the role of engineering in society and identified issues in engineering practice in the discipline, such as the professional responsibility of an engineer to public safety and sustainable development.
WK8 – Engagement with selected knowledge in the current research literature of the discipline, awareness of the power of critical thinking and creative approaches to evaluate emerging issues.

WK9 – Ethics, inclusive behavior and conduct. Knowledge of professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of engineering practice. Awareness of the need for diversity by reason of ethnicity, gender, age, physical ability etc. with mutual understanding and respect, and of inclusive attitudes.

In the department of Computer Science, the faculty’s expertise and dedication are centered on excellence in application-oriented academic teaching at the Master’s level, cooperative graduation, applied science, and cooperation with a variety of business sectors and foreign partner universities. The obsession with and excitement for potential developments based on today’s possibilities is the common thread that runs through all activities. Faculty and students of the department have been instrumental in developing and maintaining software applications ranging from Performance Evaluation System, Apps for Education, Learning Management System (Moodle), Enterprise-wide Content Management System, and various other campus-wide networking activities.

The department staff also encourages innovative projects and quality research in various interrelated domains. The department is involved in major research on which faculty members and students work in several areas such as Networks, Database, Theoretical Computer Science, Multimedia, Image Processing, Software Engineering, Data Mining, Big Data, Machine Learning, and Internet of Things.

The Industry Academia Conclave brought together a diverse array of industry experts, academics, and students to delve into the transformative impact of technology on industrial operations. Central to the discussions was the theme, "How Technology Transformed the Way Industry Works?". The panel discussion served as the focal point of the conclave, featuring esteemed panelists who shared their insights, experiences, and foresights regarding the evolving landscape of industries in the wake of technological advancements.
Key topics explored during the discussion included: Automation and Efficiency, Digitalization and Data Analytics, Industry 4.0, Skills and Workforce Development, Collaboration between Industry and Academia. Throughout the discussion, panelists elucidated on practical case
studies, best practices, and future trends, providing attendees with valuable insights into the dynamic interplay between technology and industry. The conclave concluded with a renewed sense of enthusiasm and commitment towards harnessing technology for sustainable
industrial growth and societal advancement.

The ICAM Student-Exchange Programme is a hallmark of the LCS-ICAM collaboration. So far 9 batches with a total of 151 ICAM students from 4 campuses viz., Lille, Toulouse, Paris-Senart and Nantes have visited LICET since 2011. LICET faculty members teach the 3rd semester Engineering Degree Programme as per French syllabus. Apart from their curricular requirements, students participate in various co-curricular and extracurricular activities organized by LICET, like Symposia, Project Expo, Engenia and social service. ICAM students enjoy and appreciate the immersive experience they gain during their 6-month stay at LICET, the opportunity to explore India during week-end tours and living as a member of an Indian family.

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering of Loyola-ICAM College of Engineering and Technology hosted a Special Session on ‘Recent Advances in Machine Learning and AI based Public Health Governance, Agriculture and Education’ in the 09th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development, Technically approved by IEEE Delhi Section and supported and promoted by GGSIP University, New Delhi, IETE Delhi Centre, ISTE Delhi Section, CSI Div – II, IV & CSI Delhi Chapter and IET Delhi Local Networks during 23rd– 25th March, 2022 at Bharati Vidyapeeth, New Delhi (INDIA).

The Placement and Training office is continuously striving hard to provide best training by conducting regular training programs to our students on soft skills, Aptitude, Reasoning, Quantitative, Verbal, Technical and Coding skills to form our students to be industry ready and more employable. The students are trained on the current market requirement and expectations from the companies and industries to face the challenging world to be professional and competent.

Arranging Internships, In-plant training, Industrial visits, Industrial Projects, Guest lectures, workshops and other Industry-Institute interaction activities to have practical exposure and learn more details about industrial activities. Providing Mock interviews, Group discussions, Resume building & Interview tips etc., to excel in the Placement Recruitment process. We also periodically invite our alumnus to share their success stories and motivate their juniors.

blocks.html:
College life at LICET was an experience unlike any other where lessons not only in engineering but also indispensable life lessons were embedded in us. I look at LICET and see how discipline was ensured along with kindness and love. Engineering was not a bore as we got to learn and apply in practical ways. We had our freedom but all with boundaries that should naturally be expected. We had to work and earn our internal scores, and those were ways of teaching us about honesty and hard work, that have reaped its benefits till date. The staff have guided us, encouraged us and have played a major role in our experience here. LICET has not laid impediments but built us up in all spheres. As a professional, I am grateful for the holistic approach of LICET that has laid a strong foundation for my career.

Hannah Andrew (B2013-17)

LICET provided a transformative and holistic education that balanced academic rigor with practical innovation. Through the above, I developed the technical proficiency and leadership skills necessary for my career.
I am especially grateful for the faculty at LICET for their mentorship and guidance which was instrumental in fueling my passion and my ongoing professional development.

Ashwin Balasubramanian (B 2019-2023), Google US

My time at Loyola-ICAM College of Engineering and Technology (LICET) has been an important part of my life. When I first came here, I didn’t know what to expect, but now I’m leaving with so much knowledge, new skills, and great memories.

The Computer Science and Engineering department taught me well. The professors were always helpful and pushed us to think in new ways.

The college had everything we needed – good labs, a great library, and all the right equipment. The placement team also did a great job helping us get ready for job interviews. They gave us training and made us feel confident about finding work.

College life wasn’t just about studying. We had cultural programs, festivals, and talks that helped us try new things and feel more confident. I really enjoyed working on Techczar, our department’s magazine. It taught me how to work with others, be creative, and communicate better. I had a great time working with such a wide group of people.

Most importantly, LICET helped me become a better person. I learned how to bounce back from problems, work well with teams, and lead others.

I want to thank all my teachers, friends, and everyone at LICET for helping me become who I am today. To the younger students, I say: take every chance you get, learn everything you can, and have fun during these years.

Ashley Nivedha J (B 2021-2025)
